text:
Maria: Quick thing — our Node app on PM2 is hitting the corp proxy when calling the private VPC endpoint (private.redwood.internal:8443). We set NO_PROXY but traffic still goes to proxy. Anyone seen this?
Joel: Is this from a dev laptop or a service in the same VPC?
Maria: Service running on an internal jumpbox (VPN) started with PM2. Interactive runs (node index.js) bypass the proxy fine. PM2-run processes go via proxy.
Lina: Classic env-init/order issue. PM2 might be starting before your env is exported or using a different ecosystem file. Also check spelling/format of NO_PROXY (commas, no spaces).
Maria: Our ecosystem file has: 
```
env: {
  NODE_ENV: "production",
  REDWOOD_BASE_URL: "https://private.redwood.internal:8443"
}
```
But NO_PROXY not present there. We rely on system-wide export.
Harry: PM2 inherits env from how it was started. If you started PM2 under systemd or a user session without NO_PROXY, child processes won't see it.
Joel: Another gotcha: Node HTTP/HTTPS stacks can behave differently when a request uses absolute-form vs origin-form. If the SDK generates an absolute URL (full host in the request line) the proxy is used. If it uses origin form with TLS directly to host, NO_PROXY applies. Depends on the fetch/agent.
Maria: Any way to force direct connection in our SDK? We're using the official Node client with just baseUrl passed via env.
Lina: Two practical options: (1) ensure NO_PROXY is set in the PM2 ecosystem/env before PM2 starts, or (2) pass a custom agent to the SDK that forces direct connections for the VPC host. Example (Node):
```
const https = require('https');
const directAgent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true });
const client = new RedwoodSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  baseUrl: 'https://private.redwood.internal:8443',
  fetchAgent: (url) => {
    const hostname = new URL(url).hostname;
    if (hostname.endsWith('private.redwood.internal')) return directAgent;
    return undefined; // fall back to global agent/proxy behavior
  }
});
```
Maria: Nice. We can add that as a fallback for PM2-only.
Harry: For Python folks: requests respects NO_PROXY, but if you're using urllib3 PoolManager or a custom transport you might need to set trust_env=False or pass an adapter. Example: `requests.Session()` with `session.trust_env = False` then mount a custom HTTPSAdapter.
Joel: If you need to allow NO_PROXY entries with CIDRs or subnets, Node doesn't support CIDR in NO_PROXY by default. Use explicit hostnames or implement a helper that matches IP ranges and picks the agent accordingly.
Maria: We saw reconnects failing intermittently: first connection OK, reconnect goes via proxy and fails auth (407).
Lina: That suggests the reconnect path is executed in a different process or after some library reload where env isn't set. Make sure any worker forks inherit env, or set NO_PROXY programmatically at the very top of the app before any networking module loads: `process.env.NO_PROXY = process.env.NO_PROXY ? process.env.NO_PROXY + ',private.redwood.internal' : 'private.redwood.internal'`
Maria: We added that in main and restarted PM2 — staging looks good so far. Streams hold and reconnect inline.
Harry: For debugging: tcpdump helps (see whether SYN goes to proxy IP). Also `strace -f -e trace=network` can show socket connect syscalls on linux.
Maria: Can someone capture a short checklist we can add to devex docs? Items to include: how SDK resolves baseUrl, env precedence, PM2/systemd notes, sample fetchAgent snippet, Python session.trust_env tip, tcpdump/strace debug commands.
Joel: I'll draft a short doc and open PR.
Lina: I'll review — add mention to ensure NO_PROXY uses hostnames and comma-separated values (no spaces). Also warn about wildcard/regex not being supported.
deploy-bot: PR devex/proxy-docs created and lint queued :github: 
Maria: Thanks all :pray: — this saved a deployment break.
